note: NO FACT CHANGED. The kinds list is byte-identical to 0.11.0's and no fact type gained, lost or reshaped a member. This entry records a change to the INSTRUMENT: the closed-vocabulary scan attributed membership by shape, so a gate payload's vocabularies moved this fingerprint while nothing about facts did. Membership is now declared per vocabulary and a closure check asserts nobody forgot. Scoping it surfaced three vocabularies the old scan could not see because it required a list named `All`; one of them, Classifications, travels inside every change manifest, so this is also a real increase in coverage. Classifications is a ranking and is hashed in its own order - sorted, a reordering would change what may leave a customer's network and move no ledger. A reading taken by the corrected instrument cannot reproduce one taken by the broken one, which is why this bumps rather than matching 0.11.0.

kinds: change.manifest, destination.landed, destination.pushed, environment.identity, handoff.account, loop.digest, loop.outcome, loop.transcript, source.provenance
note: NO KIND CHANGED - the list is byte-identical to 0.12.0's. What changed is a VALUE and two members. LoopMoves gains `write`, which is why this bumps at all: a member may be added freely and a value may not, because the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so an added value breaks every prior reader by design. Nothing in the vocabulary granted putting bytes at a path, so no flight could create a file - and `when: change.manifest touches migrations/**`, the gate this design is built around, most often fires on a new migration. Spelled `write` and not `create` because the tool overwrites and `create` would be a name true of one of its two uses; a new value rather than a widening of `edit`, because widening `edit` would change what an already-declared move permits for every envelope in force, retroactively, with nothing marking the day. environment.identity gains moveEnforcement and movesProbed - what this machine's executor bounds and what a startup probe proved withheld - with a new MoveEnforcements vocabulary behind the first. Not a boolean saying the bound held: the runner refuses to take work when it does not, so that member would be constant across every flight and record nothing. LoopBudget gains attempts, which is a member and costs nothing, and rides this bump rather than asking for one.

kinds: change.manifest, destination.landed, destination.pushed, environment.identity, handoff.account, loop.digest, loop.outcome, loop.transcript, source.provenance
note: NO KIND CHANGED, and that is the finding rather than an omission - the list is byte-identical to 0.13.0's. An envelope change was the first candidate for a tenth kind and it is refused on the same argument that was already recorded once: a FACT is what crosses the boundary from a runner, and an envelope change has no runner and nothing crosses. A rejection reason was ruled out as a fact for exactly this reason in slice three - appending it would make the control plane pretend to be a runner and blur the one question the evidence model answers cleanly, which is who produced this - and decisions went into EvaluableFacts as a SOURCE instead, per ADR-0011. A proposal is the same shape in every respect that matters: control-plane origin, human author, an input to evaluation rather than an observation of a flight. What moves the fingerprint is a VALUE: ExecutorRungs gains `human`, and this vocabulary is fingerprinted here because a rung is what a loop.outcome fact reports having run. Existing envelopes are unchanged in meaning - none of them named it - and a reader meeting it for the first time halts rather than deciding which rung it is.

kinds: change.manifest, destination.landed, destination.pushed, environment.identity, handoff.account, loop.digest, loop.outcome, loop.transcript, source.provenance
note: NO KIND CHANGED. The list is byte-identical to 0.14.0's; what moved is the SHAPE of destination.pushed, which gains `preserved`. It exists because slice seven separates a push from a proposal. A flight that stopped may now have its work pushed so somebody on another machine can take it over, and that push opens no pull request - so a `gg/` branch with no proposal beside it is a real state for the first time. A reader counting this platform's branches has to be able to tell work that was admitted from work that was merely kept, and those mean opposite things about whether anybody is expected to review it. A MEMBER, so no prior reader halts, and null means what it always meant: a push on the ordinary landing path. What makes it move this ledger at all is that the fingerprint covers the shape of every registered fact type, not only the list of kinds - which is the whole reason the shape is in there. A member added to a fact a runner ships is a change to what the runner may say.

kinds: change.manifest, destination.landed, destination.pushed, environment.identity, handoff.account, loop.digest, loop.outcome, loop.transcript, source.provenance
note: NO KIND CHANGED; environment.identity gains probedAt, and two existing members change meaning without moving - which is exactly what a ledger is for, because semantics do not diff. moveEnforcement is now DERIVED from the session's own probe (a held bound proves per-tool; a broken or unmeasured one ships nothing, because that lease is released with the diagnosis instead), never from an executor capability constant. movesProbed is now the set the session's probe actually held - Edit and Write, each checked against its own artifact, after slice eleven's step 0 caught substitution live. probedAt is the timestamp that makes 'a measurement of this session' auditable: the probe runs before every invocation, because ambient settings act on the session (the family's fifth member, measured the same day: --permission-mode acceptEdits defeats the bound even with setting sources cleared). full and none stay in the vocabulary as the values whose absence is the finding.
